Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki

25 min (+30 min marinate)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Marinated Skewers on the Grill

Chicken & Marinade

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, boneless150g300g450g600g
Olive oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Lemon juice15ml30ml45ml60ml
Garlic, cloves1234
Dried oregano½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Salt & pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Pita bread1234
Cherry tomatoes36912
Red onion, thin slices2468

Tzatziki

Ingredient1234
Greek yogurt60g120g180g240g
Cucumber, grated30g60g90g120g
Garlic, cloves½11½2
Fresh dill, chopped1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Lemon juice5ml10ml15ml20ml

Steps

  1. Cut the chicken into bite-sized chunks for even cooking and easy threading onto skewers.
  2. Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Toss with the chicken, cover, and marinate at least 30 minutes.
  3. Grate the cucumber, then squeeze it hard in handfuls over the sink to wring out the water — this keeps the tzatziki thick instead of watery.
  4. Stir the squeezed cucumber into the yogurt with the crushed garlic, dill, olive oil, and lemon juice. Taste and season, then chill until serving.
  5. Soak wooden skewers 15 minutes if using them, then thread the marinated chicken with a little space between pieces.
  6. Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high until a drop of water sizzles instantly.
  7. Cook the skewers 3-4 minutes per side, turning every few minutes, until golden grill marks form on every side.
  8. Check doneness by cutting into the thickest piece — it should be fully white with clear juices, no pink.
  9. Warm the pita about 20 seconds per side in the same pan until soft and slightly puffed.
  10. Plate warm pita, souvlaki skewers, a scoop of tzatziki, cherry tomatoes, and red onion. Finish with a squeeze of lemon.

Avgolemono Soup (Greek Lemon Chicken & Rice Soup)

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Tempering the Egg-Lemon Mixture

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken breast100g200g300g400g
Chicken stock300ml600ml900ml1200ml
Short/medium-grain rice20g40g60g80g
Eggs1234
Lemon juice15ml30ml45ml60ml
Salt & pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp
Fresh dill, chopped (garnish)½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp

Steps

  1. Bring the chicken stock to a boil in a pot over medium-high heat.
  2. Add the chicken breast whole and reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook 15 minutes until no longer pink in the center.
  3. Lift the chicken out onto a plate to cool slightly, keeping the stock at a simmer.
  4. Add the rice to the simmering stock and cook 12-15 minutes until fully tender.
  5. Shred the cooled chicken into bite-sized pieces with two forks.
  6. Whisk the eggs well in a heatproof bowl, then slowly whisk in the lemon juice.
  7. Ladle about a cup of hot broth into the egg-lemon mixture in a thin stream while whisking constantly — this tempers the eggs so they don't scramble.
  8. Lower the heat and slowly stir the warmed egg mixture back into the pot.
  9. Add the shredded chicken back in and stir gently 1-2 minutes over low heat until pale yellow and lightly thickened. Keep it below a boil or the eggs will curdle.
  10. Season with salt and pepper, ladle into bowls, and top with fresh dill.

Kotopoulo Lemonato (Greek Lemon Chicken & Potatoes)

1 hr 20 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Chicken and Potatoes Tossed in Lemon Marinade

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in200g400g600g800g
Potatoes, cut into wedges150g300g450g600g
Olive oil20ml40ml60ml80ml
Lemon juice30ml60ml90ml120ml
Lemon zest½ lemon1 lemon1½ lemons2 lemons
Garlic, cloves2468
Dried oregano1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Chicken stock or water60ml120ml180ml240ml
Salt & pepper¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
  2. Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, crushed garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large baking dish.
  3. Add the chicken thighs and potato wedges and toss until everything is well coated.
  4. Arrange the chicken skin-side up with the potatoes spread in a single layer around it so both can brown.
  5. Pour the stock or water around the edges of the dish, not over the chicken skin, to keep it crisp.
  6. Roast uncovered 45-55 minutes.
  7. Halfway through, baste the chicken and potatoes with the pan juices.
  8. Check doneness by cutting into the thickest piece near the bone — the meat should be fully white with clear juices (165°F/74°C on a thermometer).
  9. The potatoes are ready when a fork slides in easily and the edges look golden and crisp.
  10. Rest 5 minutes before serving so the juices settle back into the meat.

Psari Plaki (Baked Lemon-Garlic Fish with Tomatoes)

40 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Fish Fillets Topped with Tomato Sauce

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
White fish fillets (cod, halibut, or sea bass)150g300g450g600g
Tomatoes, diced (or canned)100g200g300g400g
Onion, thinly sliced¼½¾1
Zucchini or bell pepper, sliced50g100g150g200g
Garlic, cloves1234
Olive oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Lemon juice10ml20ml30ml40ml
Fresh parsley, chopped1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Salt & pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent.
  3. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
  4. Add the diced tomatoes and sliced zucchini or pepper. Simmer 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down into a chunky sauce.
  5. Pat the fish dry, season lightly with salt and pepper, and lay it in a baking dish.
  6. Pour the tomato-vegetable sauce over the fish and drizzle with lemon juice.
  7. Cover tightly with foil to trap steam and keep the fish moist.
  8. Bake covered 15 minutes, then uncover carefully and bake 5-8 minutes more.
  9. Check doneness by pressing a fork into the thickest part — the fish should flake apart easily and look opaque, not glassy.
  10. Sprinkle with parsley and serve straight from the baking dish with extra sauce spooned over.

Pastitsio (Baked Pasta with Meat Sauce & Béchamel)

1 hr 15 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Whisking the Béchamel

Meat Sauce & Pasta

Ingredient1234
Bucatini or penne pasta80g160g240g320g
Ground beef100g200g300g400g
Onion, chopped¼½¾1
Garlic, cloves1234
Crushed tomatoes (canned)100g200g300g400g
Tomato paste1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Ground cinnamonpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Olive oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Salt & pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp

Béchamel Topping

Ingredient1234
Unsalted butter15g30g45g60g
All-purpose flour15g30g45g60g
Whole milk125ml250ml375ml500ml
Egg1122
Ground nutmegpinchpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp
Grated kefalotyri or parmesan15g30g45g60g

Steps

  1. Boil the pasta 2 minutes less than the package says — it finishes cooking in the oven. Drain and set aside.
  2. Heat the olive oil and cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent.
  3. Add the garlic and ground beef, breaking it apart as it browns, 5-6 minutes until no pink remains.
  4. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered 10-15 minutes until thickened.
  5. Melt the butter in a separate saucepan over medium-low heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 1-2 minutes until it smells toasty — this is your roux.
  6. Slowly whisk in the milk to avoid lumps, then keep whisking over medium-low heat 5-7 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
  7. Off the heat, let the béchamel cool 2 minutes, then whisk in the egg, nutmeg, and grated cheese until smooth.
  8. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Layer half the pasta in a greased baking dish, the meat sauce, then the remaining pasta.
  9. Spread the béchamel evenly over the top, all the way to the edges.
  10. Bake 30-35 minutes until deep golden brown on top and bubbling at the edges.
  11. Rest at least 15 minutes before cutting into squares so it holds together.

Moussaka (Layered Eggplant & Meat Bake)

1 hr 30 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Roasting the Eggplant and Potato Slices

Vegetables & Meat Sauce

Ingredient1234
Eggplant, sliced into rounds150g300g450g600g
Potato, sliced into rounds100g200g300g400g
Ground beef or lamb100g200g300g400g
Onion, chopped¼½¾1
Garlic, cloves1234
Crushed tomatoes (canned)100g200g300g400g
Tomato paste1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Ground cinnamonpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Olive oil (for frying)15ml30ml45ml60ml
Salt & pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp

Béchamel Topping

Ingredient1234
Unsalted butter15g30g45g60g
All-purpose flour15g30g45g60g
Whole milk125ml250ml375ml500ml
Egg1122
Ground nutmegpinchpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp
Grated kefalotyri or parmesan15g30g45g60g

Steps

  1. Slice the eggplant and potato into rounds about a pencil's thickness. Salt the eggplant slices and let sit 20 minutes to pull out bitterness, then pat dry.
  2. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush both vegetables with olive oil and arrange in a single layer on baking trays.
  3. Roast 20-25 minutes, flipping halfway, until soft and lightly golden at the edges.
  4. Meanwhile, cook the onion in olive oil over medium heat 4-5 minutes until soft.
  5. Add the garlic and ground meat, breaking it apart, and cook 5-6 minutes until no pink remains.
  6. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered 10-15 minutes until thick.
  7. Make the béchamel: melt butter, whisk in flour for a roux, whisk in milk until thickened, then cool slightly and whisk in the egg, nutmeg, and cheese.
  8. Layer the roasted potatoes, then the eggplant, in a greased baking dish, and spread the meat sauce evenly on top.
  9. Pour the béchamel over everything, spreading it to the edges into a smooth blanket.
  10. Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 30-35 minutes until deep golden brown with bubbling edges.
  11. Rest at least 20 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.

Gemista (Rice-Stuffed Tomatoes & Peppers)

1 hr 30 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Filling the Hollowed Vegetables with Herbed Rice

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Large tomatoes2468
Bell peppers1234
Short/medium-grain rice, uncooked40g80g120g160g
Onion, finely chopped¼½¾1
Garlic, cloves1234
Fresh parsley, chopped1 tbsp2 tbsp3 tbsp4 tbsp
Fresh mint or dill, chopped1 tsp2 tsp1 tbsp4 tsp
Olive oil30ml60ml90ml120ml
Pine nuts (optional)5g10g15g20g
Sugarpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Salt & pepper¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers like lids and set aside. Scoop the flesh and seeds from the tomatoes into a bowl (save the pulp); discard the pepper seeds and ribs.
  3. Chop the reserved tomato pulp into small pieces.
  4. Heat the olive oil and cook the onion 4-5 minutes until soft, then the garlic 30 seconds until fragrant.
  5. Stir in the tomato pulp, uncooked rice, parsley, mint or dill, pine nuts, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook 2-3 minutes just to coat the rice — it stays hard here and finishes cooking inside the vegetables.
  6. Stand the hollowed vegetables upright, snug together, in a baking dish. Spoon in the filling, only about three-quarters full so the rice has room to expand.
  7. Replace the lids, drizzle any remaining olive oil over everything, and add a splash of water to the bottom of the dish.
  8. Cover tightly with foil and bake 45 minutes covered.
  9. Uncover and bake 30-45 minutes more, until the vegetables look soft and slightly wrinkled and the rice is fully tender.
  10. Cool 10 minutes before serving — gemista is traditionally served warm or at room temperature.

Baklava (Bonus)

1 hr (+ cooling)MediumServes 1–4

Prep — Layering Buttered Phyllo with Walnuts

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Phyllo dough sheets481216
Walnuts, finely chopped40g80g120g160g
Ground cinnamonpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Unsalted butter, melted30g60g90g120g
Sugar25g50g75g100g
Water30ml60ml90ml120ml
Honey20ml40ml60ml80ml
Lemon juice5ml10ml15ml20ml
Whole cloves (optional)1234

Steps

  1. Thaw the phyllo dough per package directions. Keep the stack covered with a lightly damp towel while working, pulling one sheet at a time.
  2. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and brush a baking dish all over with melted butter.
  3. Mix the chopped walnuts with the cinnamon.
  4. Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each one with melted butter before adding the next.
  5. Sprinkle the walnut-cinnamon mixture evenly over the buttered stack.
  6. Layer the remaining phyllo on top, buttering each sheet, finishing with a well-buttered top layer.
  7. Cut all the way through the layers into diamond or square shapes before baking — it's much harder to cut cleanly afterward.
  8. Bake 40-45 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp, not pale or soft.
  9. While it bakes, simmer the sugar, water, honey, lemon juice, and cloves (if using) 5-8 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove the cloves and let the syrup cool.
  10. Pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot baklava as soon as it comes out of the oven — cool syrup over hot pastry keeps the layers crisp instead of soggy.
  11. Let it sit uncovered at room temperature at least 4 hours, or overnight, before serving along the scored lines.
